login.title: Log in
account.title: My account: {name}
log.title: Change log
users.title: Users
users.help.html: Administrator: full access. View only: routers, charts and the whitelist without the ability to change anything; cannot see router tokens, the log or settings.
wl.title: Whitelist
wl.help.html: The router downloads the list every 5 minutes and writes it to /ip firewall address-list (list whitelist). An entry can apply to all routers or to one selected router. The router resolves domains itself through its own DNS and adds the IP addresses it finds as dynamic entries.
wl.import_help.html: One line = one entry: address,description,expiry,router. Address: IPv4, network (CIDR) or domain. Expiry: number of days or a date YYYY-MM-DD (valid until the end of that day). Description, expiry and router are optional; an unknown router name = the line is rejected. Duplicates are skipped.
rt.title: Routers
rt.name: Router name
rt.edge_help: Has a direct connection to the internet (e.g. the main router). Measures internet quality and runs the nightly speed test. Leave APs and routers behind it unchecked – they only measure the link to their own gateway.
rt.after_add: After adding, the router page opens with a configuration command to paste into the RouterOS terminal.
rt.none_admin: Add the first one and you will find its configuration command on its page.
rt.logs_title: Unacknowledged log entries from the last 24 h - click to open the logs
rt.nodata: No data, the router has not reported yet.
set.https.title: HTTPS settings
set.https.help: Requirements: the domain's DNS record points to this server, ports 80 and 443 are reachable from the internet. The certificate is obtained and renewed automatically. Leaving the domain empty = back to plain HTTP. HTTP access (e.g. for routers by IP) stays active.
set.iv.title: Monitoring interval
set.iv.dlg_1: An option for routers with spare CPU and RAM. You apply this setting at your own risk.
set.iv.dlg_2: The interval applies to all routers. At 1–5 s the database grows several to a dozen times faster (consider a shorter RETENTION_DAYS in the .env file). Watch the routers' CPU load after the change.
set.iv.after: After the change, paste the configuration command again on every router (router page → Router configuration). A shorter interval = more data in the database; charts for longer ranges are averaged.
set.wl.title: Whitelist
set.wl.help: When disabled: the Whitelist tab disappears from the menu and the configuration command does not install the sync script on routers (the list is no longer fetched every 5 minutes). After the change, paste the configuration command again on the routers. Disabling does not delete entries, neither in the panel nor on the routers.
set.sp.title: Speed test
set.sp.router: The application server is on this router's network
set.sp.na: Ookla speedtest is not available in this container.
set.sp.help_ookla: Speedtest by Ookla is built into this container: the same test as speedtest.net (download, upload, ping, jitter, packet loss, result link). The Ookla licence allows personal, non-commercial use.
set.sp.help_no.html: Ookla's program is not included in the ready-made images (licence). To use it, build the image from the source: docker compose up -d --build.
set.sp.help_tail: If the selected test fails, the fallback test (Cloudflare) is run automatically. The test runs daily at {time} and with the button on the router page (Charts → Link quality). Other edge routers run a simpler test on the router itself.
set.order.title: Router order
set.order.help: This order applies on the home page. New routers are added at the end of the list.
set.bk.title: Database backups
set.bk.noaccess.html: The backup directory is not available. Check that docker-compose.yml has the volume ./backups:/backups and run docker compose up -d.
set.bk.auto.html: Automatically every day at {hour}:00, kept for {keep} days (older ones are removed) · backups: {count} ({total})
set.bk.failed.html: The last backup attempt failed ({err}). Check: docker compose logs backup
set.bk.stale.html: No recent backup (older than 2 days or none). Check that the backup container is running: docker compose ps
set.bk.help.html: Backups are stored on the same server (the backups directory next to docker-compose.yml). For safety, download a backup to another computer from time to time. Also keep the .env file: without it (SECRET_KEY, passwords) restoring is harder. Restore instructions are in README.md.
lv.help: In setup mode the routers measure Wi-Fi and the gateway connection every 2–3 seconds. Enabling it also covers the CAPsMAN controller (it sees the clients of all APs). When the time runs out, everything returns to normal mode on its own. The router starts fast measurements within about 10 seconds.
lv.spot_ph: Spot name, e.g. Living room by the window
lv.spot_help: Stand in the spot, wait about 30 seconds and save the measurement. The average of the last 30 seconds is saved.
lv.name: Name
lv.inactive: inactive, data about once a minute
lv.stale: – the router is not sending fast Wi-Fi readings
lv.gw_empty: Will appear after setup mode is enabled.
rp.tip_dns: Median of the average latencies to 1.1.1.1, 8.8.8.8 and 9.9.9.9 from the last measurement (20 packets to each, every minute). Gateway = latency to the ISP router.
rp.tip_gw: Average latency to the upstream router from the last measurement (10 packets every 30 s).
rp.tip_loss: Loss to the DNS servers (edge router) or to the gateway (other routers) from the last measurement.
rp.ifaces_hint: current traffic · sparkline: last hour · click a row to open the chart
rp.wan_help: Daily data is recalculated every 10 minutes from the WAN interface counters; kept for about 2 years. The day is counted in local time.
rp.probes_none: No probe data. Paste the current configuration command on the router (Configuration tab).
rp.outages_help: Problem type: “no internet” – none of the servers (1.1.1.1, 8.8.8.8, 9.9.9.9) responds; “DNS not working” – the link works but name resolution does not; “HTTP not working” – web pages do not open.
rp.speed_help_srv: The test is run by the application server (same internet as this router) and measures download, upload, ping and jitter. You choose the engine in Settings → Speed test: LibreSpeed, Speedtest by Ookla (only when built from the source) or Cloudflare as a fallback. It does not load the router's CPU. Runs nightly and on demand. Takes about 40 s and uses the link for that time.
rp.speed_help_rt.html: The test is run by the router (4 parallel downloads, download only), nightly. Manually: /system script run app-speed. On weaker routers the result may be too low (HTTPS encryption loads the CPU). A more accurate test from the application server can be enabled in Settings → Speed test, if the server is on this router's network.
rp.stale_a: The data from the router is out of date (last update
rp.stale_b: ). Check the app-inventory script on the router.
rp.nodata_inv: No data. Paste the current configuration command on the router (Configuration tab); data will appear within a minute.
rp.dev_help: Online: the device sent traffic in the last few minutes (bridge host table), is connected over Wi-Fi, answers ARP or is a monitored router that is online. Idle: the router knows the device but has not seen its traffic for a long time.
rp.no_wifi: No Wi-Fi clients (or the router has no Wi-Fi).
rp.wifi_help: Quality rates the actual connection: mainly the negotiated speed relative to the maximum for the channel and number of antennas, with SNR and signal strength as supplements. Signal: green ≥ -67 dBm, yellow -67…-75, red < -75. With CAPsMAN the clients of all APs are visible on the controller.
rp.no_vpn: No WireGuard tunnels or active VPN (PPP) sessions.
rp.vpn_help: WireGuard is online when the last handshake was no more than 3 minutes ago.
rp.ack_title: Mark errors and warnings as read: resets the counter on the tab and the indicator on the home page
rp.dl_title: Download the logs from the selected period
rp.log_info: The counters on the buttons refer to the last 24 hours. At most the 300 newest entries matching the filters are shown.
rp.ana_help: The analysis translates known RouterOS messages into plain language and suggests what to do. It groups repeated events. Entries it does not recognise are at the bottom of the list.
rp.cfg_paste.html: Paste into the RouterOS terminal. In the address you can change ping= (the link test target) and add &list=list_name. After updating the application, run the command again so the router gets the new scripts.
rp.cfg_remove: Removing the configuration from the router
rp.cfg_unknown: not known yet (they will appear within a minute after pasting the command)
rp.cfg_auto: The configuration command checks on the router what is available and installs only the needed scripts (Wi-Fi new/old package, DHCP). After installing the Wi-Fi package, enabling the DHCP server or any other hardware change, paste the command again.
rp.edge_help: Check this for the router that has a direct connection to the internet (e.g. Master). Such a router measures internet quality (latency, jitter and loss to 1.1.1.1, 8.8.8.8 and 9.9.9.9, DNS and HTTP time), link availability and runs the nightly speed test. Other routers and APs only measure the connection to their gateway (the upstream router). After the change, paste the configuration command again.
rp.syslog_help: The configuration command makes the router send logs (topics critical, error, warning, info) to this server, UDP port {port}. Logs are assigned to the router by the IP address they come from.
rp.rejected: Rejected syslog packets from unknown addresses (if one of them is a router, enter that address above):
rp.confirm_clear: Delete the collected data of this router? The configuration stays.
rp.confirm_delete: Delete the router and its data?
rp.logs_empty: No logs for the selected filters. If this is a new router, paste the current configuration command (Configuration tab).
rp.err_range: The “To” date must be later than “From”.
rp.a_none_known: No recognised events in this period.
rp.avail_tip: Counted from the first measurement: {t}. Periods without data (router offline, probes not ready yet) do not lower the result.
rp.no_outages: No outages in the last 7 days.
rp.sp_none: No results. The first test will run at night.
rp.tr_none: No transfer data. The first values will appear within 10 minutes.
err.admin_required: Permission denied: this action requires the administrator role.
err.no_samples: No measurements from the last 30 s for this device.
err.speed_router: The server-side test is only available for the router selected in Settings.
msg.speed_paste: Paste the configuration command again on this router (the weaker on-router test will be disabled).
msg.wl_bad_addr: Invalid address: enter an IPv4 address, a network (e.g. 10.0.0.0/24) or a domain
msg.pw_short: The password must be at least 8 characters long.
msg.u_self: You cannot change the role of, disable or delete your own account.
msg.a_short: The new password must be at least 8 characters long.
msg.a_mismatch: The new passwords do not match.
msg.a_changed: Password changed. Other open sessions have been logged out.
msg.wl_paste: Paste the configuration command again on the routers to add or remove the sync script.
msg.bk_ok: Backup requested. It will appear in the list within about 30 seconds (refresh the page).
msg.iv_ok: Interval of {n} s saved. Paste the configuration command again on every router so it starts sending data more often.
msg.https_on: Saved. The Let's Encrypt certificate is being obtained in the background (check: docker compose logs caddy).
msg.https_off: Domain removed, only HTTP is active.
out.http: ping and DNS work, HTTP does not
an.005: lots of lost packets: weak signal or interference
an.006: the client did not respond during key exchange (often a sleeping phone or an old driver)
an.007: authentication failed: usually a wrong Wi-Fi password or a client driver problem
an.008: the client was inactive (e.g. asleep) and was disconnected
an.009: the client disconnected on its own (e.g. turned off Wi-Fi or moved to another network)
an.010: the client moved to another access point (roaming)
an.012: Someone from the internet is trying to log in to %s
an.013: Failed login attempts from addresses outside your network. These are usually automated bots that guess passwords (brute-force attack) on popular services.
an.014: Restrict the service to the local network, e.g. `/ip service set %s address=192.168.88.0/24`, disable unused services (`/ip service print`), use a strong password and a user name other than admin. Check that the firewall blocks incoming traffic from the WAN to the router.
an.018: Failed login to %s from the local network
an.019: Someone on your network entered a wrong password or user name. Single cases are usually a mistake; many attempts from one address may mean an infected device or an attempted break-in from the inside.
an.020: Check which device has this address (Devices tab). If it is not you, change the router password.
an.021: Login to the router from the internet (%s)
an.022: Someone logged in to the router from a public address, i.e. from outside your network.
an.023: Make sure it was you (e.g. remotely from work). If not, change the password immediately and restrict access to management services to the local network or a VPN.
an.025: Successful login from the local network. This is normal when managing the router, including through Winbox.
an.029: Someone changed the router settings (added, changed or removed a configuration item). This is an audit entry: it lets you check who changed what and when.
an.030: If you do not recognise the change, check it in `/log print where topics~"system"` and consider changing the password.
an.033: DHCP assigned an address to a device
an.034: A device connected to the network and got an IP address. A normal event.
an.036: A device released its DHCP address
an.037: The address lease expired or the device disconnected from the network. A normal event.
an.039: A device is not accepting an address from DHCP
an.040: The DHCP server offers an address but the device does not confirm it. The cause may be a weak Wi-Fi signal, a wrong client configuration, a second DHCP server on the network or an exhausted address pool.
an.041: Check the address pool (`/ip pool print`), whether there is a second router with DHCP enabled on the network and what signal this device has.
an.042: The DHCP pool ran out of free addresses
an.043: New devices will not get an IP address because all addresses in the pool are in use.
an.044: Enlarge the pool (`/ip pool print`, then `/ip pool set`) or shorten the lease time (lease-time).
an.045: IP address conflict on the network
an.046: Two devices use the same IP address. This can cause dropped connections.
an.047: Find the device with a manually set address from the DHCP range and change its address or add a static lease.
an.049: The port stopped seeing the other device: a disconnected cable, a powered-off device, a switch restart or a damaged cable. Frequent alternating down/up ("flapping") usually means a problem with the cable or port.
an.050: If it repeats many times on the same port, replace the cable, check the connectors and try another port.
an.052: Port linked at a reduced speed
an.053: The link works, but only at %s instead of 1 Gb/s. The usual culprit is a cable with a damaged wire, a cable that is too long or an old device on the other end.
an.054: Replace the cable with a working one (cat. 5e or better) and check the port auto-negotiation settings.
an.057: The port sees the other device again.
an.059: A device connected to the wireless network. A normal event.
an.063: If it keeps affecting the same devices: check the signal strength in the Wi-Fi tab, the distance from the AP and the radio channel. For handshake errors, check the password saved on the device.
an.066: The AP (CAP) connected to the CAPsMAN controller.
an.067: The CAPsMAN controller lost contact with the AP. The Wi-Fi network from this AP may have stopped working.
an.068: Check the AP power (PoE), the cable and whether the AP is visible on the network.
an.069: Router started after an improper shutdown
an.070: The router was not shut down normally: most often a power loss, a pulled plug or a system crash (freeze).
an.071: If it repeats without power losses, check the power supply and temperature and download the autosupout.rif file from Files (crash report) for MikroTik support. Consider a UPS.
an.073: The router started again (manually, after an update or from a schedule).
an.074: If you did not restart it, check in the logs who was logged in before the restart.
an.075: the application server was temporarily not responding (e.g. during an update)
an.076: the router could not connect to the server
an.077: the script contains a command not supported by this RouterOS version
an.078: the script ended with an error
an.080: A script run on the router (e.g. this application's monitoring or whitelist) did not run correctly.
an.081: Single errors during an application update are normal. If they keep repeating, paste the configuration command again (Configuration tab) and check that the router can see the server.
an.082: Connection attempts from the internet to the %s service on the router
an.083: A firewall rule with logging registered packets from the internet addressed to port %s (%s). These are usually automated scans looking for open services.
an.084: Make sure these packets are dropped (a drop rule for WAN traffic) and that the service is not exposed to the internet unnecessarily.
an.087: A firewall rule registered a packet (%s)
an.088: This is an entry from a firewall rule that has logging enabled (log=yes). It shows where the traffic came from and where it went.
an.089: If there are very many such entries, disable logging in the rule or add a log-prefix to tell them apart.
an.092: The router lost its PPPoE connection to the ISP, so there was no internet for that time.
an.093: If it happens often, check the cable to the modem/ONT and report the problem to the ISP (give the times from the logs).
an.094: WireGuard: no connection to the other end of the tunnel
an.095: The handshake with the peer did not complete. The other side is off, has no internet, or the keys or endpoint address are wrong.
an.096: Check in the VPN tab which peer it concerns, and its public key and address.
an.098: Excessive broadcast/multicast traffic is appearing on the port, which usually means a cable connects two ports of the same switch or two switches are connected twice.
an.099: Check the cabling of the indicated port and enable RSTP on the bridge (`/interface bridge set [find] protocol-mode=rstp`).
an.101: The PoE port detected an overload, a short circuit or too high a power draw by the powered device.
an.102: Check the cable and the device powered from this port, and the router power supply limit.
an.104: The router ran out of memory. Services may run unstably or the router may restart.
an.105: Check the RAM usage on the chart, disable unnecessary features (e.g. large address lists, proxy) or update RouterOS.
an.125: Changes to RouterOS Monitor scripts and schedules
an.126: Traces of this application's configuration on the router: pasting the configuration command adds and removes app-… scripts and tasks, and RouterOS logs every such change. They may also be your own manual changes to the app-… schedules (e.g. disabling the whitelist synchronisation).
an.127: Nothing needs to be done. If you did not paste the command or change anything, check who was logged in.
an.129: Someone changed the router settings. RouterOS records who, with what (e.g. Winbox) and from which address made the change, and which command was run.
an.130: If you do not recognise the change or the user, change the password and check the user list (`/user print`).
an.131: Script content fragments in the log (after pasting the configuration command)
an.132: When the configuration command adds app-… scripts, RouterOS writes the whole command with the script body to the log. Long entries are split into many pieces, hence the code fragments in the logs. These are not errors.
an.133: Nothing needs to be done. They appear only when the configuration command is pasted.
an.134: the old Wi-Fi package `wireless`, which does not exist on routers with the new `wifi` package (ax models)
an.135: the new Wi-Fi package `wifi`, which does not exist on this router
an.136: the `/system health` menu, which does not exist on this model (no sensors)
an.137: the command `%s` is not available in this RouterOS version or on this model
an.138: syntax not supported by this RouterOS version
an.139: A script uses a command not available on this router
an.140: The script refers to: %s. RouterOS aborts such a script when loading it.
an.141: If this is an app-… script of this application, paste the current configuration command again (Configuration tab); newer versions run only the scripts that match the router. A custom script has to be fixed manually.
an.143: The %s script ended with an error
an.146: RouterOS writes this entry together with the actual error (usually the line next to it in the log). By itself it only indicates which script did not run.
an.147: Check the neighbouring entry with the error description. For app-… scripts: single cases (e.g. during an application update) are normal; permanent errors are fixed by pasting the configuration command again.
an.149: Whitelist synchronisation with the application server
an.150: The router downloaded a file from %s
an.151: The app-whitelist script fetches the current whitelist from this application every 5 minutes. Each fetch leaves this entry, so there are about 288 a day.
an.152: The router downloaded a file with the `/tool fetch` command (a script or a manual command).
an.153: The new configuration command no longer sends these entries to the application. On the router you can also silence them in its own log: `/system logging set [find action=memory topics=info] topics=info,!fetch`. If you do not use the whitelist on this router, disable the task: `/system scheduler disable [find name=app-wl]`.
an.156: The router could not download the file (server unavailable, network error or wrong address).
an.157: If this is the application server, check that it is running (`docker compose ps`) and that the router can see it.
an.158: AP connected to the CAPsMAN controller
an.159: This access point (CAP) connected to the CAPsMAN controller %s and is fetching its Wi-Fi configuration from it.
an.162: The access point found the CAPsMAN controller %s on the network and selected it for management. An entry about the connection usually appears a moment later.
an.163: AP lost its connection to the CAPsMAN controller
an.164: The access point disconnected from the controller %s. Wi-Fi from this AP may not have worked during that time.
an.165: If it repeats, check the AP's cable connection to the network and whether the CAPsMAN controller was available (restart, update).
an.172: The router clock was set by %s.
an.173: The difference was large, so the times in earlier logs may have been wrong (e.g. after restarting a router without a clock battery).
an.174: Small corrections of a few to a few dozen seconds are normal.
an.175: For accurate time enable the NTP client: `/system ntp client set enabled=yes servers=pool.ntp.org`. Correct time is important for logs, certificates and schedules.
an.176: Router got an IP address from DHCP
an.177: Router lost its IP address from DHCP
an.178: The router itself (as a DHCP client on interface %s) got an address from a DHCP server on the network, e.g. an AP from the main router or a router from the ISP. This is not an address being assigned to another device.
an.179: The router's DHCP client on interface %s lost its address: the DHCP server did not respond or the link was unavailable.
an.180: Check the connection on this interface and the availability of the DHCP server (e.g. the main router or the ISP modem).
an.183: Package %s version %s was installed on the router, usually as part of a system update (the entry appears after a restart).
an.184: Package %s %s was removed from the router.
an.185: After updating RouterOS also upgrade the board firmware: `/system routerboard upgrade`, then restart the router (the panel shows a “firmware to upgrade” badge if needed).
an.187: Password attack (brute force) from the internet
an.188: Many failed login attempts from the same public addresses (most: %d). This is an automated attack that guesses the password.
an.189: Unstable link on a port (frequent disconnects)
set.sp.help_ls: LibreSpeed (the default in the ready-made image) is an open-source test (LGPL) run against the public community servers of librespeed.org; it does not send your results to anyone. The servers vary in quality, so by default the best one according to a short test is used. For more accurate measurements of fast links use Speedtest by Ookla (after building the image yourself).
err.ls_missing: LibreSpeed is not available in this container.
set.sp.best_info: The program compares the few nearest servers with a short download test (about 5 s each) and uses the fastest one for measurements. Community servers differ in bandwidth, so the nearest is not always the best. The choice is repeated every 7 days and uses a few dozen seconds of traffic; no results are sent anywhere.
set.sp.best_none: Not checked yet. The first test or the button below will do it.
set.sp.best_busy: Another test is running, try again in a moment.
bl.title: Blacklist
bl.help.html: The router downloads the list every 5 minutes and writes it to /ip firewall address-list (list blacklist). An entry can apply to all routers or to one selected router, with an expiry date (temporary ban) or without. The list alone blocks nothing: you need the firewall rule shown below.
bl.rule_help: Paste once on each router in the RouterOS terminal (a rule in the raw table runs before connection tracking, so it is light on the CPU). Firewall rule order decides: if whitelisted addresses must never be blocked, add an accept rule for them before this rule. After pasting the router's configuration command again the list entries refresh on their own.
msg.bl_self: You cannot ban the address you are using right now, the application server or a monitored router.
msg.bl_broad: Network too broad: the largest allowed is /8.
msg.bl_bad: This address cannot be added to the blacklist (loopback, multicast, reserved or IPv6).
set.bl.title: Blacklist
set.bl.help: When disabled: the router does not get the blacklist sync script (the list is no longer fetched every 5 minutes). After the change, paste the configuration command again on the routers. Disabling does not delete entries, neither in the panel nor on the routers, and you remove the blocking rule on the router yourself.
set.bk.limit_fits: the {limit} limit holds about {n} backups (the newest is {size}); older ones are removed automatically and the newest is always kept
set.bk.too_big: The newest backup ({size}) is larger than the limit, so it is kept; raise the limit to keep more backups.
set.bk.low_disk: Low free disk space ({free}). Consider setting a backup size limit.
msg.bk_limit_bad: Enter a limit from 0.1 GB to 100000 GB.
